assignedReviews.card_evidence: avoid turning rocks over, avoid trampling plants and animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about shore visit etiquette and environmental conservation, with no mention of volcanoes, their formation, or any volcanic activity. It does not support the competency 'explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed' in any way.

copy.en: When visiting the shore, avoid turning rocks over, avoid trampling plants and animals, and take only photographs while leaving only footprints.
copy.tl: Kapag bumibisita sa dalampasigan, iwasang baligtarin ang mga bato, iwasang tapakan ang mga halaman at hayop, at kumuha lamang ng mga larawan habang nag-iiwan lamang ng mga bakas ng paa.
copy.bis: Kung mobisita sa baybayon, likayi ang pagbaliskad sa mga bato, likayi ang pagtamak sa mga tanom ug mananap, ug pagkuha lamang og mga litrato samtang nagbilin lamang og mga tunob sa tiil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Volcanic aerosol cooling is short-term
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses volcanic aerosol cooling and its spatial effects, which is an Earth/climate science topic. It provides no information about physical properties of solid materials such as hardness, shininess, or stretchability.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Volcanic aerosol cooling is short-term
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about volcanic aerosol cooling, not about forces changing the shape of objects. It does not address pushing, pulling, stretching, bending, twisting, or squeezing.

copy.en: Volcanic aerosol cooling is short-term and spatially uneven, meaning some areas cool down while others may even experience warmer conditions.
copy.tl: Ang paglamig mula sa volcanic aerosol ay panandalian lamang at hindi pantay-pantay sa iba't ibang lugar, ibig sabihin may mga lugar na lumalamig habang ang iba ay maaaring mas uminit pa.
copy.bis: Ang pagpabugnaw tungod sa volcanic aerosol hamubo lamang ug dili parehas sa lain-laing lugar, nagpasabot nga adunay mga lugar nga mobugnaw samtang ang uban mahimong mas moinit pa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Displacement is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of an object
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the physics concept of displacement (shortest straight-line distance), which is unrelated to the competency about levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere. The tag is a clear subject mismatch.

copy.en: Displacement is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of an object, so it is always a straight line.
copy.tl: Ang displacement ay ang pinakamaikling distansya mula sa initial hanggang sa final position ng isang bagay, kaya ito ay palaging tuwid na linya.
copy.bis: Ang displacement mao ang pinakamubo nga distansya gikan sa initial ngadto sa final position sa usa ka butang, busa kini kanunay nga tul-id nga linya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A shrub is different from a herb because a shrub has a woody or hard stem, while a herb has a soft stem.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the difference between shrubs and herbs based on stem hardness. G6-E-8 requires making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to explain seasons, star patterns, and eclipses. There is no connection to Earth-Sun-Moon motions or any astronomical content.

copy.en: A shrub is different from a herb because a shrub has a woody or hard stem, while a herb has a soft stem.
copy.tl: Ang shrub ay naiiba sa herb dahil ang shrub ay may woody o matigas na tangkay, habang ang herb ay may malambot na tangkay.
copy.bis: Ang shrub lahi sa herb tungod kay ang shrub adunay woody o gahi nga punoan, samtang ang herb adunay humok nga punoan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During Storm Signal No. 2
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes effects of a storm signal (tilted coconut trees, unroofed houses), which is weather-related content. G3-M-7 requires demonstrating proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties (reusing, recycling, etc.). There is no instructional support for material handling or disposal.

copy.en: During Storm Signal No. 2, some coconut trees may tilt or break, and many nipa and cogon houses may be partially or totally unroofed.
copy.tl: Sa Storm Signal No. 2, ang ilang puno ng niyog ay maaaring tumagilid o mabali, at maraming bahay na nipa at cogon ang maaaring masiraan ng bubong.
copy.bis: Sa Storm Signal No. 2, ang uban nga lubi mahimong motagilid o mabali, ug daghan nga balay nga nipa ug cogon ang mahimong maguba ang atop.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Single replacement reactions are used in silver plating
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models or illustrations to explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes and identify and explain which types of faults are most likely to occur in the Philippines and explain why
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a chemistry single-replacement reaction in silver plating; it has no content about faults, earthquakes, or Philippine fault types.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Single replacement reactions are used in silver plating
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a chemical reaction, not plate boundaries, their structures, movements, or events.

copy.en: Single replacement reactions are used in silver plating, where copper replaces silver in a compound, causing silver crystals to form on the copper.
copy.tl: Ang single replacement reactions ay ginagamit sa silver plating, kung saan pinapalitan ng copper ang silver sa isang compound, na nagiging sanhi ng pagbuo ng silver crystals sa copper.
copy.bis: Ang single replacement reactions gigamit sa silver plating, diin ang copper mopuli sa silver sa usa ka compound, nga nagpahinabo sa pagporma sa silver crystals sa copper.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Prokaryotic cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: Card describes prokaryotic cells (biology), while competency concerns drawing/modeling Earth-Moon-Sun motion to explain moon phases. No instructional support.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Prokaryotic cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: Card describes prokaryotic cells, unrelated to observing Sun, Moon, planets, and stars moving across the sky.

copy.en: Prokaryotic cells are simple cells without a true nucleus or membrane-bound organelles, found in bacteria and archaea.
copy.tl: Ang mga prokaryotic cell ay mga simpleng cell na walang tunay na nucleus o membrane-bound organelles, na matatagpuan sa bacteria at archaea.
copy.bis: Ang mga prokaryotic cells mga simple nga cells nga walay tinuod nga nucleus o membrane-bound organelles, nga makita sa bacteria ug archaea.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the chemistry concept of empirical formula (e.g., CH2O for glucose). It provides no information about constructing or labeling speed graphs, stationary/uniform speeds, or fast/slow speeds.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe uniform velocity and represent it using distance-time graphs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about empirical formulas in chemistry, not about uniform velocity or distance-time graphs. It does not support any part of the motion competency.

copy.en: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound, like CH2O for glucose.
copy.tl: Ang empirical formula ay nagpapakita ng pinakasimpleng whole-number ratio ng mga atom sa isang compound, tulad ng CH2O para sa glucose.
copy.bis: Ang empirical formula nagpakita sa pinakasimple nga whole-number ratio sa mga atom sa usa ka compound, sama sa CH2O alang sa glucose.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The receptor cells in the skin send messages to the brain, and the brain controls the sweat glands of the body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes skin receptors sending messages to the brain and the brain controlling sweat glands. This is about the human nervous and integumentary systems, with no connection to earthquakes, their magnitude, or their effects on communities. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated.

copy.en: The receptor cells in the skin send messages to the brain, and the brain controls the sweat glands of the body.
copy.tl: Ang mga receptor cells sa balat ay nagpapadala ng mensahe sa utak, at kinokontrol ng utak ang mga sweat glands ng katawan.
copy.bis: Ang mga receptor cells sa panit nagpadala og mensahe ngadto sa utok, ug gikontrol sa utok ang mga sweat glands sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The skin is the body's first barrier — it blocks germs from getting inside before they can make us sick.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. The card discusses the skin as a barrier against germs, which is not one of the listed systems and does not support the competency.

copy.en:
What blocks germs from entering us first?

The skin is the body's first barrier — it blocks germs from getting inside before they can make us sick.
copy.tl:
Ano ang unang harang sa mga mikrobyo?

Ang balat ang unang harang ng katawan — pinipigilan nito ang mga mikrobyo na makapasok bago pa tayo magkasakit.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang unang babag sa mga mikrobyo?

Ang panit mao ang unang babag sa lawas — gipugngan niini ang mga mikrobyo nga makasulod sa wala pa kita masakit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ancient people believed the sky and Earth were connected, so they watched heavenly bodies like the sun, moon, and stars to tell time and know the seasons.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ancient beliefs about the sky and Earth and using heavenly bodies for timekeeping and seasons. G9-L-7 is about class discussion of threats to biodiversity leading to species extinction. There is no biodiversity, extinction, or threat content, so the tag is unrelated.

copy.en: Ancient people believed the sky and Earth were connected, so they watched heavenly bodies like the sun, moon, and stars to tell time and know the seasons.
copy.tl: Naniniwala ang mga sinaunang tao na magkaugnay ang langit at lupa, kaya pinagmamasdan nila ang mga heavenly body tulad ng araw, buwan, at mga bituin para malaman ang oras at panahon.
copy.bis: Mituo ang mga karaan nga mga tawo nga konektado ang langit ug yuta, busa ilang gibantayan ang mga heavenly body sama sa adlaw, bulan, ug mga bituon aron mahibaloan ang oras ug panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your brain sorts and stores what you learned that day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains sleep's role in memory consolidation. It does not describe growth, response, or reproduction, which are the characteristics of living things in G3-L-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your brain sorts and stores what you learned that day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses memory storage during sleep and contains no labeled diagram or content about levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere.

copy.en:
Why does sleep help you remember lessons?

While you sleep, your brain sorts and stores what you learned that day — that's why lessons stick better after a good night's sleep!
copy.tl:
Bakit tumutulong ang tulog para maalala ang aral?

Habang natutulog ka, inaayos at iniimbak ng utak ang natutunan mo sa araw na iyon — kaya mas naaalala mo ang aral pagkatapos ng magandang tulog!
copy.bis:
Nganong makatabang ang tulog aron mahinumdoman ang leksyon?

Samtang natulog ka, hapsayon ug tipigan sa utok ang imong nakat-onan nianang adlawa — mao nga mas mahinumdoman nimo ang leksyon human sa maayong tulog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An earthquake intensity of II, Slightly Felt, is felt by few individuals at rest indoors, and hanging objects swing slightly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an earthquake intensity scale (PHIVOLCS Intensity II), which is a geology/earth science topic. It provides no information about basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An earthquake intensity of II, Slightly Felt, is felt by few individuals at rest indoors, and hanging objects swing slightly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about earthquake intensity, not about characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). No direct or prerequisite support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An earthquake intensity of II, Slightly Felt, is felt by few individuals at rest indoors, and hanging objects swing slightly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses earthquake intensity, not the difference between living and non-living things. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: An earthquake intensity of II, Slightly Felt, is felt by few individuals at rest indoors, and hanging objects swing slightly.
copy.tl: Ang intensity ng lindol na II, Slightly Felt, ay nararamdaman ng iilang tao na nagpapahinga sa loob ng bahay, at ang mga nakasabit na bagay ay bahagyang umuuga.
copy.bis: Ang intensity sa linog nga II, Slightly Felt, mabati sa pipila ka mga tao nga nagpahulay sa sulud sa balay, ug ang mga gibitay nga butang gamay nga mag-uyog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The slope of an inclined plane is the vertical change, called the rise, divided by the horizontal change, called the run.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate and describe the relationship among the projectile variables including the angle and velocity of release, and projectile height and range, using everyday activities such as shooting basketballs or kicking footballs
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines the mathematical slope of an inclined plane (rise over run). G10-F-1 requires investigating and describing relationships among projectile variables (angle and velocity of release, projectile height and range) using everyday activities. The card provides no information about projectile motion, launch variables, or their relationships, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: The slope of an inclined plane is the vertical change, called the rise, divided by the horizontal change, called the run.
copy.tl: Ang slope ng inclined plane ay ang vertical change, na tinatawag na rise, na hinati sa horizontal change, na tinatawag na run.
copy.bis: Ang slope sa inclined plane mao ang vertical change, nga gitawag ug rise, nga gibahin sa horizontal change, nga gitawag ug run.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inner planets have diameters less than 13,000 kilometers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the sizes of inner planets, which is unrelated to the competency about how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Inner planets have diameters less than 13,000 kilometers, making them much smaller than the outer giants.
copy.tl: Ang mga inner planet ay may diameter na mas mababa sa 13,000 kilometers, kaya mas maliit sila kaysa mga outer giant.
copy.bis: Ang mga inner planet adunay diameter nga ubos sa 13,000 kilometers, busa mas gagmay sila kay sa mga outer giant.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can compare objects and arrange them in order from the smallest to the largest
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain the harmful effects that EMR can have on living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches comparing and ordering objects by size, which is unrelated to the competency about explaining harmful effects of electromagnetic radiation on living things.

copy.en: You can compare objects and arrange them in order from the smallest to the largest, like lining up leaves by size.
copy.tl: Maaari mong paghambingin ang mga bagay at ayusin ang mga ito mula sa pinakamaliit hanggang sa pinakamalaki, tulad ng paghahanay ng mga dahon ayon sa laki.
copy.bis: Mahimo nimong itandi ang mga butang ug ipahiluna kini sugod sa pinakagamay hangtod sa pinakadako, sama sa paglinya sa mga dahon base sa gidak-on.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Different liquids have different smells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the smell of liquids, which is a property of matter, not weather observation or recording. It does not support the competency about observing and recording weather changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Different liquids have different smells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about liquid smells, unrelated to examining a local weather chart, interpreting weather, or practicing safety precautions for poor weather. No connection to the competency.

copy.en: Different liquids have different smells, like the strong smell of alcohol and the sweet smell of perfume.
copy.tl: Iba-iba ang amoy ng mga liquid, tulad ng matapang na amoy ng alcohol at mabangong amoy ng pabango.
copy.bis: Lahi-lahi ang baho sa mga liquid, sama sa kusog nga baho sa alcohol ug humot nga baho sa pahumot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cigarette smoke has many different effects on the circulatory system, including contributing to the hardening of arteries and other blood vessel diseases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local impacts of global climate change and suggest ways that individuals can do to reduce the impact of global warming
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the health effects of cigarette smoke on the circulatory system. The competency G10-E-11 is about identifying local impacts of global climate change and suggesting ways to reduce global warming. There is no connection between smoking and climate change; the card does not support any part of the competency.

copy.en: Cigarette smoke has many different effects on the circulatory system, including contributing to the hardening of arteries and other blood vessel diseases.
copy.tl: Ang usok ng sigarilyo ay may maraming iba't ibang epekto sa circulatory system, kabilang ang pag-aambag sa paninigas ng mga artery at iba pang sakit sa ugat ng dugo.
copy.bis: Ang aso sa sigarilyo adunay daghang lain-laing epekto sa circulatory system, lakip na ang pag-amot sa paggahi sa mga artery ug uban pang sakit sa ugat sa dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Burning dried leaves, paper, tires, and plastics releases dirty smoke into the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses air pollution from burning; it does not use diagrams or illustrations, nor does it describe particle arrangement, spacing, or motion in the three states of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Burning dried leaves, paper, tires, and plastics releases dirty smoke into the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the Particle Model of Matter as 'All matter is made up of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles.'
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not mention the Particle Model of Matter, tiny particles, or pure substances; it is about pollution from burning, not about the particle nature of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Burning dried leaves, paper, tires, and plastics releases dirty smoke into the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases); it only mentions smoke as a pollutant without teaching the states of matter.

copy.en: Burning dried leaves, paper, tires, and plastics releases dirty smoke into the air, causing pollution that makes the air unsafe to breathe.
copy.tl: Ang pagsusunog ng tuyong dahon, papel, gulong, at plastic ay naglalabas ng maruming usok sa hangin, na nagdudulot ng pollution at ginagawang hindi ligtas ang hanging nilalanghap.
copy.bis: Ang pagsunog sa uga nga dahon, papel, ligid, ug plastic nagpagawas ug hugaw nga aso sa hangin, nga hinungdan sa pollution ug naghimo sa hangin nga dili luwas nga maginhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: smoking is banned in many public places to protect everyone's health.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a public smoking ban and general health protection. It does not identify or describe any parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: smoking is banned in many public places to protect everyone's health.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a smoking ban policy, not about describing how any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) works. It provides no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: In the Philippines, smoking is banned in many public places to protect everyone's health.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, ipinagbabawal ang paninigarilyo sa maraming pampublikong lugar upang maprotektahan ang kalusugan ng lahat.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, gidili ang pagpanigarilyo sa daghang pampublikong lugar aron mapanalipdan ang panglawas sa tanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: soap lifts the oils where germs cling
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about soap removing oils and germs during washing. It does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, nor any mixture classification. The topic is hygiene, not mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: soap lifts the oils where germs cling
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify a solute or solvent in a solution. It discusses soap's action on oils and germs, with no mention of solution components or roles. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Washing with soap works much better than water alone — soap lifts the oils where germs cling, so the water can rinse them away.
copy.tl: Mas mabisa ang paghuhugas gamit ang sabon kaysa tubig lang — tinatanggal ng sabon ang langis kung saan nakakapit ang mikrobyo, kaya mas madali itong matangay ng tubig.
copy.bis: Mas epektibo ang panghugas gamit ang sabon kay sa tubig ra — makuha sa sabon ang lana diin nagkapyot ang mikrobyo, mao nga mas sayon kining mabanlasan sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Since one end of soap clings to water, the flowing rinse drags away all the trapped dirt and oil from your skin.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why rinsing soap removes dirt and oil, but it does not demonstrate or describe any mixture separation technique such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, or using magnets. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Just rubbing soap isn't enough; you must rinse! Since one end of soap clings to water, the flowing rinse drags away all the trapped dirt and oil from your skin.
copy.tl: Hindi sapat na ipahid lang ang sabon; kailangan itong banlawan! Dahil kumakapit sa tubig ang isang dulo ng sabon, tinatangay ng daloy ang lahat ng nakulong na dumi at langis mula sa balat.
copy.bis: Dili igo nga ipahid lang ang sabon; kinahanglan kining banlawan! Tungod kay mokupot sa tubig ang usa ka tumoy sa sabon, gidala sa dagayday ang tanang nakulong nga hugaw ug lana gikan sa panit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not from making soap! They're extra ingredients mixed in afterward
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that soap color and scent are added ingredients, not that they form uniform or non-uniform mixtures. It does not describe solutions, suspensions, or any mixture classification, so it does not support G6-M-4.

copy.en:
Where does soap get its pretty color and nice smell?

Not from making soap! They're extra ingredients mixed in afterward to make soap look and smell amazing.
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang magandang kulay at mabangong amoy ng sabon?

Hindi galing sa paggawa ng sabon! Mga dinagdag na sangkap lang 'yan na inihahalo pagkatapos para mas maganda at mabango ang sabon.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang nindot nga kolor ug humot nga baho sa sabon?

Dili gikan sa paghimo sa sabon! Dugang nga mga sangkap ra na nga gisagol human aron mas nindot ug humot ang sabon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their combined velocity is found by dividing the ball's momentum by their total mass
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses momentum and velocity in a soccer catch, a physics topic. G8-M-4 is about pure substances, elements/compounds, and protons, which is chemistry/matter content. There is no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: When a soccer player catches a ball and slides with it, their combined velocity is found by dividing the ball's momentum by their total mass.
copy.tl: Kapag sinalo ng soccer player ang bola at dumausdos kasama nito, ang kanilang pinagsamang velocity ay makukuha sa pamamagitan ng paghahati ng momentum ng bola sa kanilang kabuuang mass.
copy.bis: Kon saloon sa soccer player ang bola ug modahili uban niini, ang ilang gihiusa nga velocity makuha pinaagi sa pagbahin sa momentum sa bola sa ilang total nga mass.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sodium hydroxide, also called lye, is a strong base found in drain cleaners and oven cleaners because it can dissolve grease and hair.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sodium hydroxide as a strong base used in cleaners. It has no connection to Philippine seasons or seasonal activities, which is the subject of G6-E-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sodium hydroxide, also called lye, is a strong base found in drain cleaners and oven cleaners because it can dissolve grease and hair.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a chemical substance and its use in cleaners. It does not address solar energy, breezes, monsoons, or the ITCZ, which are the focus of G7-E-12.

copy.en: Sodium hydroxide, also called lye, is a strong base found in drain cleaners and oven cleaners because it can dissolve grease and hair.
copy.tl: Ang sodium hydroxide, na tinatawag ding lye, ay malakas na base na matatagpuan sa mga drain cleaner at oven cleaner dahil kaya nitong tunawin ang mantika at buhok.
copy.bis: Ang sodium hydroxide, nga gitawag usab og lye, usa ka kusgan nga base nga makita sa mga drain cleaner ug oven cleaner tungod kay kaya niyang matunaw ang mantika ug buhok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why is sodium nitride written as Na3N?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the ionic bonding and formula of sodium nitride (Na3N), a chemistry topic. G6-E-5 requires interpreting PHIVOLCS volcano monitoring alert levels and demonstrating actions before, during, and after a volcanic eruption. There is no connection to volcanoes, alert levels, or safety procedures.

copy.en:
Why is sodium nitride written as Na3N?

One nitrogen atom needs three electrons to fill its outer shell, so three sodium atoms each donate one electron, forming Na3N.
copy.tl:
Bakit isinusulat ang sodium nitride bilang Na3N?

Ang isang nitrogen atom ay nangangailangan ng tatlong electron upang mapuno ang kanyang outer shell, kaya tatlong sodium atom ang bawat isa ay nagdo-donate ng isang electron, na bumubuo ng Na3N.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang sodium nitride gisulat isip Na3N?

Ang usa ka nitrogen atom nagkinahanglan og tulo ka electron aron mapuno ang iyang outer shell, busa tulo ka sodium atom ang matag usa nagdonate og usa ka electron, nga nagporma og Na3N.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil is a non-renewable resource, so once it is eroded, it cannot be renewed

assignedReviews.reason: Soil as non-renewable is earth science, not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil is a non-renewable resource, so once it is eroded, it cannot be renewed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Soil erosion is unrelated to how plants reproduce.

copy.en:
Can soil grow back after it erodes?

No! Soil is a non-renewable resource, so once it is eroded, it cannot be renewed.
copy.tl:
Maaari bang tumubo muli ang lupa pagkatapos ma-erode?

Hindi! Ang lupa ay non-renewable resource, kaya kapag na-erode na ito, hindi na ito maibabalik.
copy.bis:
Makatubo ba pag-usab ang yuta human ma-erode?

Dili! Ang yuta usa ka non-renewable resource, mao nga kon ma-erode na kini, dili na kini mabalik.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work

copy.en: Soil erosion happens when wind or water carries away topsoil, and it can reduce the land's ability to grow plants and support agriculture.
copy.tl: Ang soil erosion ay nangyayari kapag tinatangay ng hangin o tubig ang pang-ibabaw na lupa, at nababawasan nito ang kakayahan ng lupa na magpatubo ng halaman at suportahan ang agrikultura.
copy.bis: Ang soil erosion mahitabo kon ang hangin o tubig magdala sa ibabaw nga yuta, ug mokunhod ang abilidad sa yuta sa pagpatubo sa tanom ug pagsuporta sa agrikultura.

copy.en: Soil health, or how good the soil is for growing, influences which crops farmers choose and how they take care of their fields.
copy.tl: Ang soil health, o kung gaano kaganda ang lupa para sa pagtatanim, ay nakakaapekto sa kung anong pananim ang pipiliin ng mga magsasaka at kung paano nila aalagaan ang kanilang mga bukirin.
copy.bis: Ang soil health, o kung unsa ka maayo ang yuta alang sa pagtanom, makaapekto sa unsa nga tanom ang pilion sa mga mag-uuma ug unsaon nila pag-atiman sa ilang mga uma.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses physical states in chemical equations, not typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone.

copy.en:
What do the little letters (s), (l), (g), and (aq) mean in an equation?

They are state symbols that tell the physical form: solid, liquid, gas, or aqueous, which means dissolved in water!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng maliliit na letrang (s), (l), (g), at (aq) sa isang equation?

Ang mga ito ay state symbol na nagsasabi ng pisikal na anyo: solid, liquid, gas, o aqueous na ibig sabihin natunaw sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buot ipasabot sa gagmay nga mga letra nga (s), (l), (g), ug (aq) sa usa ka equation?

Kini mga state symbol nga nagsulti sa pisikal nga porma: solid, liquid, gas, o aqueous nga nagpasabot natunaw sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A solstice is when the Sun is at its greatest distance from the equator.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe some of the materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a solstice and its relation to seasons and day length. G6-E-4 requires identifying and describing materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines. The card has no volcanic content and is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
What is a solstice?

A solstice is when the Sun is at its greatest distance from the equator. It marks the start of summer or winter and gives the longest or shortest day!
copy.tl:
Ano ang solstice?

Ang solstice ay kapag ang Araw ay nasa pinakamalayong distansya mula sa equator. Ito ang nagmamarka sa simula ng summer o winter at nagbibigay ng pinakamahaba o pinakamaikling araw!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang solstice?

Ang solstice mao kung ang Adlaw anaa sa pinakalayo nga distansya gikan sa equator. Kini ang nagtimaan sa sinugdanan sa summer o winter ug naghatag sa pinakataas o pinakamubo nga adlaw!

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses human impact on ecosystems and mitigation solutions (planting trees, waste disposal). It does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) as required by G3-L-6.

copy.en: Articles about human impact on ecosystems can provide evidence and suggest solutions, like planting trees and proper waste disposal, to reduce negative effects.
copy.tl: Ang mga artikulo tungkol sa epekto ng tao sa ecosystem ay nagbibigay ng ebidensya at nagmumungkahi ng solusyon, tulad ng pagtatanim ng puno at tamang pagtatapon ng basura, para mabawasan ang masamang epekto.
copy.bis: Ang mga artikulo mahitungod sa epekto sa tawo sa ecosystem naghatag ug ebidensya ug nagsugyot ug solusyon, sama sa pagtanom ug kahoy ug hustong paglabay sa basura, aron mamenosan ang daotang epekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Using Ohm's law, R = V/I = 12 V / 0.50 A = 24 ohms!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how solar energy contributes to the occurrence of land and sea breezes, monsoons, and the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches solving for electrical resistance using Ohm's law, which is unrelated to the competency about solar energy causing land/sea breezes, monsoons, and ITCZ. The assigned code is a clear mismatch.

copy.en:
What is the resistance if a 12-volt battery pushes 0.50 amperes?

Using Ohm's law, R = V/I = 12 V / 0.50 A = 24 ohms!
copy.tl:
Ano ang resistance kung ang 12-volt na battery ay nagtulak ng 0.50 amperes?

Gamit ang Ohm's law, R = V/I = 12 V / 0.50 A = 24 ohms!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang resistance kung ang 12-volt nga battery nagtulak ug 0.50 amperes?

Gamit ang Ohm's law, R = V/I = 12 V / 0.50 A = 24 ohms!

copy.bis: Ang sound energy makapahinabo og mga kausaban, sama sa paghimo og tingog sa mga instrumento sa musika ug pagpasa sa impormasyon pinaagi sa komunikasyon.

copy.bis: Ang sound energy gigamit alang sa kaluwasan, sama sa busina sa sakyanan nga nagpahimangno sa mga tawo nga adunay moabot nga sakyanan.

copy.bis: Ang Adlaw mao ang pangunang tinubdan sa kahayag para sa mga anino sa Earth, pero ang flashlight, kandila, ug lampara makahimo usab og kahayag ug anino.

copy.bis: Ang South American Plate ug African Plate nagporma og divergent boundary, mao nga ang South America nagpalayo sa Africa.

copy.en: Gas particles have large spaces between them, which is why gases can expand to fill any container and be easily compressed into a smaller space.
copy.tl: Ang mga gas particle ay may malalaking espasyo sa pagitan nila, kaya ang gas ay maaaring lumawak para punuin ang anumang lalagyan at madaling ma-compress sa mas maliit na espasyo.
copy.bis: Ang mga gas particle adunay dagkong mga espasyo tali kanila, mao nga ang gas makapalapad aron mapuno ang bisan unsang sudlanan ug daling ma-compress ngadto sa mas gamay nga espasyo.

copy.en: Species richness is the simplest measurement of species diversity, relating to the number of species inhabiting a given area or habitat.
copy.tl: Ang species richness ay ang pinakasimpleng sukat ng species diversity, na tumutukoy sa bilang ng species na naninirahan sa isang lugar o tirahan.
copy.bis: Ang species richness mao ang pinakasimple nga sukod sa species diversity, nga nagtumong sa gidaghanon sa mga species nga nagpuyo sa usa ka lugar o puy-anan.
